**Revolut secures conditional US bank charter from OCC**

*Conditional approval to form a national bank clears the hardest regulatory hurdle for Europe's most valuable fintech, setting up a direct presence in the world's largest financial market by 2027.*

The US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted Revolut preliminary conditional approval on September 2 to organise as a branchless digital bank headquartered in Stamford, Connecticut, under the name Revolut Bank US, National Association. The charter, published as Corporate Decision #1390, would allow Revolut to hold federally insured deposits, issue credit cards and personal loans, and access Federal Reserve payment systems directly – ending its reliance on partner banks for US operations.

Revolut filed its charter application in March, led by US CEO Cetin Duransoy, a former Capital One and Raisin US executive appointed when the application was submitted. The OCC's conditional approval letter requires an initial capital contribution of at least $95 million. Revolut, which serves more than 80 million customers globally and is valued at $75 billion, has said it expects to launch the US bank in the first half of 2027.

Conditional approval is not a final green light. Revolut must still obtain deposit insurance from the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation and approval from the Federal Reserve before the bank can open. Clearing the OCC stage is widely regarded as the most demanding part of the process – and comes after Wise, another London-based fintech, had its own US trust charter application rejected by the OCC earlier this year on anti-money-laundering grounds.

*Sources: [Revolut wins conditional approval for US bank charter](https://www.fintechfutures.com/regulatory-actions/revolut-wins-conditional-approval-for-us-bank-charter) — FinTech Futures*

**Pay.UK warns AI-driven fraud is the fastest-moving threat to UK payments**

*AI-enabled scams are advancing faster than the rule-based defences most UK banks rely on, sharpening the case for coordinated industry investment in real-time, AI-powered detection.*

Pay.UK has identified AI-driven fraud as the most rapidly evolving threat to the UK payments system, signalling that the sophistication and speed of AI-enabled attacks are outpacing the detection capabilities currently deployed across the sector.

The warning arrives against a backdrop of rising UK fraud losses. Total payment fraud losses reached £1.3 billion in figures published in June, with authorised push payment scams accounting for £576.4 million of that total. The Payment Systems Regulator's mandatory reimbursement regime has shifted the financial burden squarely onto sending banks. AI is accelerating that problem: deepfake voice and video scams, AI-generated phishing and automated social engineering are all becoming harder to intercept with rule-based monitoring systems.

Pay.UK's position as operator of Faster Payments gives its assessment particular weight. The organisation's framing of AI fraud as a systemic rather than institution-level risk adds pressure on banks and payment service providers to invest in real-time, AI-powered defences – and exposes gaps in regulatory frameworks that were designed around older, slower forms of financial crime.

*Sources: [ECB and Brazil explore cross-border link between TIPS and Pix](https://paymentsindustryintelligence.com/ecb-and-brazil-explore-cross-border-link-between-tips-and-pix/) — Paymentsindustryintelligence*

**BRICS summit report proposes interoperable digital payments and open finance framework**

*Cross-border payment corridors that European providers depend on could be reshaped by a BRICS+ recommendation for common technical standards and interoperable national payment systems.*

Delegates preparing for the 2026 BRICS summit in Delhi have produced a report recommending a BRICS+ Digital Payments and Open Finance Framework, built on interoperable national payment systems and common technical standards. The proposal would create a structured pathway for connecting fast-payment systems across member nations.

The framework builds on existing bilateral efforts – notably the ECB-Banco Central do Brasil exploration of linking TIPS to Pix, and China's mBridge project – but aims to formalise cross-border payment interoperability at a multilateral level. BRICS+ now encompasses economies responsible for a substantial share of global remittance flows, and a coordinated approach to payment system interoperability would create alternative corridors to those dominated by Western card networks and correspondent banking chains.

European payment providers and infrastructure operators face a strategic question: whether BRICS+ interoperability develops as a complement to existing global standards such as ISO 20022 and Swift, or as a parallel architecture that fragments cross-border payments further. The proposal's emphasis on common technical standards suggests alignment is possible, but the geopolitical context makes divergence equally plausible.

*Sources: [BRICS 2026: India braces to host Xi, Putin in Delhi as it seeks to project voice of developing ...](https://www.fortuneindia.com/india/brics-2026-india-braces-to-host-xi-putin-in-delhi-as-it-seeks-to-project-voice-of-developing-economies/157903) — Fortuneindia*

**Lean Technologies raises $67.5m to scale open banking across MENA**

*The Series B round, led by General Catalyst, is the largest open banking funding in the Middle East and signals growing investor confidence in non-European open finance markets.*

Lean Technologies, a Riyadh-based open banking and pay-by-bank provider, is raising $67.5 million in Series B funding led by General Catalyst. The capital will support expansion of its open banking and pay-by-bank offerings across the Middle East and North Africa.

The round is notable for its size relative to the MENA open banking market, which remains earlier-stage than its European and UK counterparts. Saudi Arabia's open banking framework, overseen by the Saudi Central Bank, has been operational since 2023, and the UAE's Central Bank has been issuing open finance licences at an accelerating pace – NymCard received its third regulatory approval from the UAE central bank in the same week.

For European open banking firms eyeing geographic expansion, the MENA region represents both opportunity and competition. Several European providers, including Yapily and TrueLayer, have explored or entered Middle Eastern markets, and Lean's funding suggests that well-capitalised local players are building defensible positions. The involvement of General Catalyst, a major US venture firm, also reflects broader investor appetite for open banking infrastructure outside the saturated UK and EU markets.

*Sources: [Riyadh fintech Lean Technologies raises $67.5M Series B led by General Catalyst](https://app.dealroom.co/news/feed/riyadh-fintech-lean-technologies-raises-67-5m-series-b-led-by-general-catalyst) — Dealroom*
